```{r setup, include=FALSE}
# Keep output tidy
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)

# Core packages
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
```


```{r file-paths}

data_dir <- here("data/r_practice_tidy_data_joins")

birds_file    <- file.path(data_dir, "52_pp52_birds_1.csv")
surveys_file  <- file.path(data_dir, "52_pp52_surveys_1.csv")
sites_file    <- file.path(data_dir, "52_pp52_sites_1.csv")
taxalist_file <- file.path(data_dir, "52_pp52_taxalist_1.csv")

# Quick check
file.exists(c(birds_file, surveys_file, sites_file, taxalist_file))
```

## 2) Read in the data (Question 1)

This creates the required objects with the required names.

```{r read-data}
bird_observations <- readr::read_csv(birds_file, show_col_types = FALSE)
surveys           <- readr::read_csv(surveys_file, show_col_types = FALSE)
sites             <- readr::read_csv(sites_file, show_col_types = FALSE)
taxalist          <- readr::read_csv(taxalist_file, show_col_types = FALSE)
```

```{r glimpse-tables}
glimpse(bird_observations)
glimpse(surveys)
glimpse(sites)
glimpse(taxalist)
```

---

## 4) (Optional) quick relational checks

These are handy because these datasets are meant to join on IDs.


```{r id-checks}

# How many unique IDs?
bird_observations %>% summarise(n_sites = n_distinct(site_id),
                               n_surveys = n_distinct(survey_id),
                               n_species = n_distinct(species_id))

surveys %>% summarise(n_sites = n_distinct(site_id),
                      n_surveys = n_distinct(survey_id))

# Check whether survey IDs in birds exist in surveys
anti_join(
  bird_observations %>% distinct(survey_id),
  surveys %>% distinct(survey_id),
  by = "survey_id"
) %>% nrow()

# Check whether species IDs in birds exist in taxalist
anti_join(
  bird_observations %>% distinct(species_id),
  taxalist %>% distinct(species_id),
  by = "species_id"
) %>% nrow()
```
